closest.title: Ensemble Adversarial Training: Attacks and Defenses
closest.how_close: Direct methodological overlap: improves robustness by augmenting training with adversarial perturbations transferred from other models. However, it targets image classifiers, rather than diffusion-based manipulation policies, and does not establish the proposed combination of diverse diffusion noise schedules, physical patches, and curriculum training.

closest.title: How vulnerable is my policy? Adversarial attacks on modern behavior cloning policies
closest.how_close: Studies diffusion policies on manipulation tasks, including offline universal perturbations and transfer across algorithms, architectures, and tasks. Its evaluated defense is randomized smoothing; it does not adversarially train policies using transferable ensemble perturbations or physical patches.

closest.title: Curriculum Adversarial Training
closest.how_close: Already develops adversarial training with a curriculum of increasing attack strength while retaining clean-input performance. The target is image classification, and it does not implement diffusion-policy ensembles or combined digital and physical-patch training.

rationale: No paper outside the supplied bibliography was found implementing the full proposed combination: hardening diffusion-based manipulation policies through transferable ensemble-generated perturbations, digital and simulated physical-patch adversarial training, and an attack curriculum. Nevertheless, close methodological precedents exist: Ensemble Adversarial Training already trains against perturbations transferred from other models, and Curriculum Adversarial Training supplies the progressive attack-strength mechanism. The closest target-specific paper studies transferable attacks on diffusion policies but uses a different defense. These are substantial partial overlaps, supporting a score of 3 rather than an exact-duplication judgment. Ref-005 was excluded from the closest papers and scoring as requested.
